cards.text: It's the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the day the Passover lamb is sacrificed. Jesus' disciples ask Him where He wants them to prepare for Him to eat the Passover. Big holiday meal and no location yet, friend, which is every family group chat in history.
So Jesus sends two of them into the city, and the directions are basically: somebody's gonna meet you. Friend, I live on a planet with ONE building, and I have never given directions that confident.

cards.question: Jesus sends two disciples into the city to find the place for the Passover. Who does He say will meet them there?

answers.text: A man carrying a jug of water
A man leading a young donkey
A woman drawing water at a well

cards.text: Follow him, Jesus says, and tell the owner of whatever house he walks into: "The Teacher asks: Where is My guest room, where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?"

cards.question: Jesus says the owner of the house will show the two disciples a room for the Passover. What kind of room?
True or false: When the two disciples get to the city, things don't go the way Jesus described.

cards.text: They find everything just as Jesus described, the room furnished and ready, and they prepare the Passover. Meanwhile, I once gave a baker directions to my sprinkles, and they came back forty minutes later holding a spatula.
When evening comes, Jesus arrives with the Twelve. They're reclining, they're eating, and then Jesus says something I bet nobody at that table saw coming.

cards.question: In the middle of the Passover meal, Jesus says one of the people eating with Him will do something. What?
When Jesus says one of them will betray Him, the disciples begin to be ___ and ask Him one after another if He means them.

cards.text: One after another: "Surely not I?" It's like the boss saying somebody in this office messed up, and suddenly the whole team is replaying every email they sent this week.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says the one who will betray Him is someone from outside the Twelve.

cards.text: It's one of the Twelve, Jesus says, the one dipping his hand into the bowl with Him. Same bowl, friend, that close.

cards.question: Jesus says the Son of Man will go just as it is written about Him. What does He say about the man who betrays Him?

answers.text: Better for him if he'd never been born
He'll be driven out of the land forever
His name will be wiped from every record

cards.text: While they're still eating, Jesus takes bread, speaks a blessing, breaks it and hands it to the disciples. I bet the room gets quiet, friend.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples to take the bread He just broke. He says the bread is His ___.

cards.text: Then He takes the cup, gives thanks and hands it to them, and they all drink from it.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples what the cup they just drank from is. What does He call it?

cards.text: "This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many." Then Jesus makes a promise about the next time He'll drink of the fruit of the vine.

cards.question: Jesus says He won't drink of the fruit of the vine again until the day He drinks it anew. Where does He say that will be?

cards.text: They sing a hymn and head out to the Mount of Olives. My little Sparkle used to hum to the oven while it warmed up, and the first time I tried it here in my bakery, my oven turned itself OFF.

cards.question: Out at the Mount of Olives, Jesus tells the disciples what all of them are going to do. What does He say?

answers.text: They will all preach in Jerusalem

cards.text: Jesus points to what is written: "I will strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered." Hard news, but He's not done talking.

cards.question: After the hard news, Jesus gives the disciples a promise. He says that after He has ___ He will go ahead of them into ___.

cards.text: Peter, one of the Twelve, isn't having it: "Even if all fall away, I never will." That's me at night setting a 5 a.m. alarm, FULLY convinced tomorrow's me is a morning person.

cards.question: Peter just promised he'll never fall away. What does Jesus say Peter will do this very night?
True or false: Jesus tells Peter it will all happen before the rooster crows once.

cards.text: Peter keeps insisting: "Even if I have to die with You, I will never deny You."

cards.question: True or false: While Peter insists he'll never deny Jesus, the rest of the disciples stay quiet.

cards.text: We're pulling this batch out of the oven right here, friend. Keep that apron on, because this story is far from done.

findings.problem: The card says 'I bet nobody at that table saw coming' Jesus' announcement of a betrayer. The provided previous passage (Mark 14:10-11) shows Judas had already gone to the chief priests and agreed to hand Jesus over, so Judas, who was at that table, did see it coming. Even marked as a guess, the line says something the text shows is wrong. It should be reworded, for example 'I bet most of that table didn't see this coming.'

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'relieved' isn't a believable reaction to hearing that one of them will betray Jesus, and it doesn't match the tone of the other answers. It works as a throwaway, so the card gets easier and the choice is between only two real options. It should be replaced with a believable feeling that the text doesn't support, such as 'confused' or 'afraid'.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: No earlier card mentions the rooster, and nothing sets up how many times it crows. The baker can only guess whether 'once' is right, so the pick comes down to luck. The stop already has several discovery questions (the jug of water, the upper room, Galilee). Either a story card should give context before this card, or the card should ask something the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
